overview: This batch focuses on finalizing the ultra-endgame state by implementing deterministic compression for the 5,500-tick simulation history and optimizing the Monte Carlo survival rate calculation for near-instantaneous replay verification. These steps ensure the simulation remains lightweight and verifiable without cascading dependencies.

tasks.title: Implement Deterministic Bit-Packed State Compression for Tick History
tasks.architectural_spec: Use std::array<uint64_t, 1024> for fixed-size storage. Implement a static constexpr function packState(const TickState&) that maps enum values and integer counters into bit-fields within uint64_t. No dynamic allocation. Use std::bit_cast for type punning. Ensure all operations are constexpr-friendly where possible.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: 1. Compression ratio > 85% for 5,500 ticks. 2. Decompression is O(1) per tick. 3. Zero heap allocations during pack/unpack. 4. Unit tests verify bit-exact reconstruction.
tasks.player_fun_impact: Faster load times for saved games and smoother scrubbing through simulation history.

tasks.title: Optimize Monte Carlo Survival Rate Calculation with SIMD
tasks.architectural_spec: Utilize std::simd (C++20) for parallel accumulation of survival flags. Process 16,500 footsteps in chunks of 16. Use alignas(64) for data structures. Implement a static constexpr function calculateSurvivalRate(const std::span<const bool>&) that returns a float. Avoid branching in the inner loop.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: 1. Calculation completes in < 1ms for 16,500 entries. 2. Result matches scalar implementation exactly. 3. No dynamic memory allocation. 4. SIMD intrinsics are used via std::simd.
tasks.player_fun_impact: Instantaneous feedback on simulation stability during gameplay.
